findings.title: Persist parsed token data rather than the safeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns { success: true, data: tokens }, whereas the previous schema.parse returned the tokens themselves. Saving that wrapper as credential.key removes the top-level access_token and refresh_token expected by googleCredentialSchema. Even with credential sharing disabled, the first successful refresh corrupts the stored credential and subsequent Google Calendar service construction fails. Save the result's data property instead.

findings.title: Computed schema keys do not preserve expiry or token fields
findings.body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal object-property name, not a wildcard. Both computed keys resolve to '[object Object]', and z.object strips undeclared properties. With sharing enabled, valid responses therefore lose expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other provider fields. For example, Zoom computes its new expiry from an undefined expires_in and overwrites its refresh token with the placeholder. Define explicit fields and preserve required provider metadata instead.

findings.title: Normalize the sync response for SDK and Axios callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several converted callers expect a different return shape: Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM and Bigin read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint. Enabling syncing consequently breaks refreshes for these integrations. Parse the response and adapt it to each caller's contract, or change all callers to a consistent contract.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy value
findings.body: The helper injects the literal 'refresh_token' even when sharing is disabled. Office365's refresh response schema deliberately permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Previously this preserved the existing refresh token; now a successful response without a replacement overwrites it with an unusable string, causing the next refresh to fail. Leave absent refresh tokens absent so callers can retain the existing value.

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce refresh
findings.body: The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without type checking, throws ReferenceError after every successful Salesforce token refresh, preventing the connection from being created.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: Unlike the other integrations, Salesforce now unconditionally refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com and never calls refreshOAuthTokens. In sharing mode the parent application is supposed to own refreshes and return access tokens; credentials without a locally usable refresh token will fail here even if the configured sync endpoint can supply a valid token. This also refreshes on every connection construction rather than using the existing valid access token.

findings.title: Pass the user ID rather than the credential ID to syncing
findings.body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is sent to the parent application as calcomUserId, but Bigin passes credentialId. Credential and user IDs are independent, so the endpoint will look up a nonexistent user or return another user's credentials when the numbers coincide. Thread credential.userId through refreshAccessToken and pass that instead; team credentials should retain the null user ID so they use the local refresh path.

findings.title: Use Zoom's app slug in the sync request
findings.body: The sync request sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are registered with appId='zoom' in the OAuth callback and the incoming webhook resolves apps by their database slug. A parent application using those same slugs cannot resolve this refresh request. Pass 'zoom' rather than the integration directory name.

findings.title: Serialize credential creation for concurrent webhook deliveries
findings.body: The findFirst followed by create is not atomic. Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no credential can both observe no row and create separate credentials. Later deliveries update only one arbitrary matching row, leaving the other credential stale and available to integration consumers. Protect the lookup/create operation with appropriate database serialization or an idempotency mechanism so retries cannot create duplicate installations.
